bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 59.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content-moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on platforms that host user-generated content.
Online publishers and digital media platforms may face compliance obligations if they host user-generated intimate content.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. It would require websites and apps that host user-generated content to remove such images within 48 hours of being notified by the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 466.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research grants and regulatory pathways for development of drugs and therapies targeting ALS and neurodegenerative diseases.
Providers treating ALS patients may see changes in available investigational therapies and clinical trial access, though the bill focuses primarily on research and regulatory processes.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data on experimental drugs and mandates that the Food and Drug Administration publish a five-year plan describing how it will help develop and approve therapies for these rare diseases. The bill also continues a public-private partnership between federal agencies and outside organizations working on neurodegenerative disease treatments.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: New Era of Preventing End-Stage Kidney Disease Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The bill establishes new training programs and centers of excellence that would operate within hospitals and health systems.
Research into rare kidney disease diagnosis, treatment, and alternatives to dialysis would directly affect medical device and pharmaceutical development in nephrology.
Health professions schools would receive funding to establish fellowship programs and expanded training curricula for kidney disease care.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create federally funded regional centers focused on rare kidney diseases, require certain medical schools to offer fellowships in rare kidney disease care for underserved populations, and expand primary care training programs to include kidney disease education. It also directs the Department of Health and Human Services to study rare kidney disease treatment, dialysis alternatives, and public awareness strategies and report findings to Congress.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers working with controlled substances and affects the regulatory classification of fentanyl-related compounds.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect defense attorneys and prosecutors handling drug trafficking cases.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and makes it easier for registered researchers to conduct certain activities without additional permits.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service relating to "Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the San Francisco Bay-Delta Distinct Population Segment of the Longfin Smelt".

industries.rationale: Endangered species protections in the Bay-Delta region directly affect water allocation for agricultural irrigation in California's Central Valley.
Water management and hydroelectric operations in the Bay-Delta system face regulatory constraints when species are listed as endangered.
Water utilities and water districts must comply with endangered species protections that affect pumping, diversion, and discharge operations in the Bay-Delta.
Development projects near Bay-Delta waterways face additional permitting requirements and habitat mitigation when endangered species are present.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a federal rule that listed a specific population of longfin smelt fish in the San Francisco Bay-Delta region as endangered. If passed, the fish would lose protections under the Endangered Species Act that were granted in July 2024. The resolution uses a congressional review process that allows lawmakers to nullify recently issued federal regulations.

plain.whoItTouches: People who keep animals, and people who work with them.

bill.title: Providing congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Advanced Clean Cars II; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".
subjects: Hybrid, electric, and advanced technology vehicles

industries.rationale: Automotive manufacturers face different emission and zero-emission vehicle requirements depending on whether California's waiver stands or is revoked.
Zero-emission vehicle mandates directly affect demand for gasoline and diesel fuel in California's large vehicle market.
Electric vehicle adoption rates influence demand for charging infrastructure and electricity from renewable sources.
The pace of electric vehicle deployment affects electricity demand and grid infrastructure investment needs.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would cancel a federal waiver that allows California to enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II regulations. Those regulations set stricter standards for vehicle emissions and require automakers to sell more zero-emission vehicles in California. If the resolution passes, California would lose the authority to enforce these stricter rules, reverting to federal emission standards.

bill.title: Providing congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Heavy-Duty Vehicle and Engine Emission Warranty and Maintenance Provisions; Advanced Clean Trucks; Zero Emission Airport Shuttle; Zero-Emission Power Train Certification; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects regulatory obligations for trucking companies and heavy-duty vehicle operators subject to California emission standards.
The bill would change compliance requirements for manufacturers of heavy-duty trucks and engines sold in California.
Revoking zero-emission truck mandates would reduce market requirements for electric vehicle charging infrastructure and clean powertrain technology.
Changes to zero-emission vehicle requirements could affect electricity demand and infrastructure planning for fleet electrification.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would cancel waivers that allow California to enforce its own stricter emission standards for heavy-duty trucks and engines. Under the Clean Air Act, California can request permission to set its own vehicle pollution rules that are tougher than federal standards; this resolution would revoke several such waivers related to truck emissions, warranties, zero-emission airport shuttles, and advanced clean truck requirements. If passed, California would lose the authority to enforce these particular state-level vehicle pollution rules.

bill.title: Providing congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine and Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; The "Omnibus" Low NOX Regulation; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".
subjects: Hybrid, electric, and advanced technology vehicles

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects emissions compliance obligations for manufacturers and operators of heavy-duty trucks, buses, and diesel-powered vehicles and equipment.
Vehicle and engine manufacturers would face different regulatory requirements depending on whether California's stricter emissions standards remain in effect or are preempted by federal rules.
Construction firms use off-road diesel equipment covered by the waiver, and the bill would affect compliance costs and equipment specifications for these machines.
Agricultural operations use off-road diesel engines and heavy-duty vehicles subject to the emissions standards that would be affected by revoking the waiver.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would cancel a waiver that allows California to enforce stricter emissions standards than federal rules for heavy-duty trucks, buses, and off-road diesel equipment starting with 2024 models. The waiver, granted by the Environmental Protection Agency under the Clean Air Act, permits California to set its own limits on nitrogen oxide pollution from these vehicles and engines. If passed, the resolution would restore federal preemption and prevent California from enforcing these particular state-level standards.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
